He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He was a consensus five-star prospect, and one of the top-rated basketball players in the class of 2017. He won the [[2019 NBA All-Star Game|2019]] [[Slam Dunk Contest]]. ==High school career== Diallo attended [[John Bowne High School]] in [[Flushing, New York]] during his freshman and sophomore year. He also attended [[Putnam Science Academy]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 17.1 points, 6.6 rebounds per game, and 2.7 assists. During the 2015 summer, Diallo competed on the [[Under Armour]] Association Circuit (UAA) for the AAU team, New York Jayhawks, where he averaged 22.5 points and 5.0 rebounds per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2015/08/24/kentucky-will-track-2017-guard-hamidou-diallo/|title=Kentucky Will Track 2017 Guard Hamidou Diallo|date=August 24, 2015|website=Zagsblog.com|access-date=April 2, 2021}} Later that summer Diallo was invited to both NBPA Top 100 and [[Adidas]] Nations camps.{{Cite web|url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/adidas-nation-what-we-learned|title=Adidas Nations: What we learned|last=Bossi|first=Eric|date=August 4, 2015|website=rivals.com|access-date=April 2, 2021}}{{Cite web|url=https://hoopseen.com/news/general/201506/nba-top-100-camp-top-sgs|title=NBPA Top 100: Top SGs|last=Young|first=Justin|date=June 22, 2015|website=Hoopseen.com|access-date=March 4, 2020}} Diallo transferred to Putnam Science Academy in [[Putnam, Connecticut]] prior to his junior year. As a junior, he averaged 17.0 [[points per game]], and 4.0 rebounds while leading Putnam to a (35–7) overall record. In the 2016 summer, Diallo then joined the AAU team, New York Rens on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) Circuit. He averaged 18.6 points, and 2.1 assists while leading the Rens to the season-ending Peach Jam. As a senior in 2016–17, he averaged 19.0 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 3.0 assists where he led the Mustangs to a (38–3) record. Diallo was considered one of the top players in the 2017 recruiting class by [[Scout.com]], [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/story/1712117-hamidou-diallo-is-eligible-for-the-nba-draft|title=Hamidou Diallo is eligible for the nba draft, will consider all options|last=Daniels|first=Evan|date=September 29, 2016|access-date=November 5, 2016|via=Scout.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161103164532/http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/story/1712117-hamidou-diallo-is-eligible-for-the-nba-draft|archive-date=November 3, 2016|url-status=dead}}{{Cite news |title=Hamidou Diallo, Putnam science Academy SG – Scout |url=http://www.scout.com/player/195220-hamidou-diallo |access-date=January 7, 2017 |via=scout.com}}{{Cite news |title=Hamidou Diallo - Rivals.com |url=http://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/1734 |access-date=January 7, 2017 |via=rivals.com}} Diallo was heavily recruited by six schools: [[University of Kentucky]], [[University of Arizona]], [[Indiana University]], [[University of Kansas]], [[Syracuse University]], and the [[University of Connecticut]].{{Cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=November 21, 2016 |title=Will five-star Hamidou diallo bypass college for NBA? |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/insider/post?id=116462 |access-date=April 30, 2023 |via=ESPN.com}} ==College career== On January 7, 2017, Diallo committed to the [[University of Kentucky]].{{Cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=January 7, 2017 |title=Hamidou Diallo, No. 11 in ESPN 100, picks Kentucky over UConn |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/18427587 |access-date=April 30, 2023 |via=ESPN.com}} He [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]], graduating a semester early and joining the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Wildcats]] midseason that month.{{cite news|first=John|last=Marshall|title=Duke recruit Bagley raises issue of 'reclassification'|date=August 19, 2017|work=Austin American-Statesman|url=https://www.statesman.com/story/news/2017/08/19/duke-recruit-bagley-raises-issue-of-reclassification/10378356007/|access-date=May 30, 2022}} He would start participating with the team in practices, but would not play a single game that year due to his late entry into the program. Diallo was one of a record-high 182 players to declare for the [[2017 NBA draft]], despite not having played a single college game in the process. On May 24, 2017, Diallo announced that he would return to Kentucky to play in their [[2017–18 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2017–18 season]], despite draft scouts saying he could have been taken in the first round of the draft that year.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19456982|title=Kentucky's Hamidou Diallo will return for freshman season|last=Goodman|first=Jeff|date=May 24, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=April 7, 2021}} Diallo had season averages of 10.0 points and 3.6 rebounds per game. ==Professional career== ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2018–2021)=== [[File:Hamidou Diallo - 2018 NBA Summer League.png|thumb|left|150px|Diallo at the [[2018 NBA Summer League]]]] On June 21, 2018, Diallo was selected with the 45th pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. His draft rights were subsequently traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]],{{cite web |date=June 20, 2018 |title=Reports: Charlotte Hornets trade Dwight Howard to Brooklyn Nets |url=https://www.nba.com/news/report-charlotte-hornets-trade-dwight-howard-brooklyn-nets |access-date=August 10, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} and then to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/diallo-180706|title=Thunder Acquires Hamidou Diallo|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018}} On July 28, 2018, the Thunder announced that they had signed Diallo to his [[NBA salary cap|rookie-scale contract]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/diallo-180728|title=Thunder Signs Hamidou Diallo|date=July 28, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 28, 2018}} On October 16, 2018, Diallo made his debut in NBA, coming off the bench in a 100–108 loss to the [[2018–19 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]] with four points, a rebound, an assist and a steal.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070214|title=Curry, Durant lead Warriors past Thunder in festive opener|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2018|access-date=October 18, 2018}} On November 19, 2018, Diallo scored a career-high 18 points with two steals, a rebound, and an assist in a 113–117 loss to the [[2018–19 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070928|title=Buddy Hield helps Kings turn back Russell Westbrook, Thunder|work=ESPN.com|date=November 19, 2018|access-date=November 20, 2018}} On February 16, 2019, Diallo won the [[NBA Slam Dunk Contest]], becoming the first Oklahoma City Thunder player ever to win it. For one dunk he jumped over [[Shaquille O'Neal]], and did the "honey dip" dunk popularized by [[Vince Carter]], and displayed a [[Superman]] undershirt while hanging from the rim. In another dunk, he jumped over rapper [[Quavo]] who held the ball above his head and finished it with two hands.{{Cite web |last=Newport |first=Kyle |date=February 17, 2019 |title=Hamidou Diallo Wins 2019 NBA Slam Dunk Contest; Full Scores and Reaction |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2821146-hamidou-diallo-wins-2019-nba-slam-dunk-contest-full-scores-and-reaction |access-date=February 17, 2019 |website=Bleacher Report}} ===Detroit Pistons (2021–2023)=== On March 13, 2021, Diallo was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk]] and a future second-round draft pick.{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Hamidou Diallo From Oklahoma City Thunder In Exchange For Svi Mykhailiuk and Future Second-Round Pick|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-hamidou-diallo-oklahoma-city-thunder-exchange-svi-mykhailiuk-and-future|website=NBA.com|date=March 13, 2021|access-date=March 13, 2021}} On August 19, 2021, Diallo signed a two-year, $10.4 million rookie-scale extension with the Pistons.{{cite web|title=Pistons re-sign Hamidou Diallo following breakout season|url=https://www.nba.com/news/piston-re-sign-hamidou-diallo-following-breakout-season|website=NBA.com|date=August 20, 2021|access-date=March 25, 2022}} On March 25, 2022, he was ruled out for the remainder of the [[2021–22 Detroit Pistons season|2021–22 season]] with an [[avulsion fracture]] in his left index finger.{{cite web|title=Pistons' Hamidou Diallo (finger) to miss rest of season|url=https://www.nba.com/news/pistons-hamidou-diallo-finger-to-miss-rest-of-season|website=NBA.com|date=March 26, 2022|access-date=March 25, 2022}} On December 29, 2022, Diallo was suspended by the NBA for one game without pay due to an altercation during a game against the [[2022–23 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]] the day before.{{cite web|title=NBA announces suspensions from Pistons-Magic game|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-announces-pistons-magic-suspensions|website=NBA.com|date=December 29, 2022|access-date=December 31, 2022}} On March 6, 2023, during a 110–104 loss to the [[2022–23 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]], he suffered a right ankle injury. The next day, the Pistons announced that Diallo had suffered a grade 2 sprain in his right ankle and would be re-evaluated in three to four weeks.{{cite tweet|first=Omari|last=Sankofa II|title=Hamidou Diallo is essentially out for the season with a Grade 2 right ankle sprain. Tough break|number=1633230512989917185|user=omarisankofa|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}} In a press conference the same day, however, Pistons head coach [[Dwane Casey]] stated that Diallo would miss the rest of the [[2022–23 Detroit Pistons season|2022–23 season]].{{cite tweet|first=James L.|last=Edwards III|title=Casey said Diallo is the only one who he knows will be done for the season. Said the medical staff will "keep an eye" on Bogey and Burks moving forward.|number=1633231126566240257|user=JLEdwardsIII|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}} ===Washington Wizards / Capital
